subject: bug with num.threads>1 on a Mac

messages.author: 55d0e2f87b0f795e
messages.subject: bug with num.threads>1 on a Mac
parts:
Hi R-inla group, 

I seem to have found a bug that occurs on my 8-core Mac when I use more than 1 thread, but it doesn't occur on my coworker's 4-core Linux computer. I see in the documentation that num.threads defaults to 1 in Windows; maybe it should on a Mac too? I get inconsistent and inaccurate fixed effect estimates when I use the default or if I specify num.threads=6. I get consistent and decent estimates if I only use 1 core. I didn't try it with intermediate numbers of cores. If I reduce the number of observations and random effect levels, the bug goes away. This is the example. 

library(INLA)


simfun0 <- function(beta=c(2,1),

                   sd.re=5,

                   ngrp=10,nobs=200,

                   invlink=exp) {

    x <- rnorm(nobs)

    f <- factor(rep(1:ngrp,nobs/ngrp))

    u <- rnorm(ngrp,sd=sd.re)

    eta <- beta[1]+beta[2]*x+u[f]

    mu <- invlink(eta)

    return(data.frame(x,f,mu))

}

#ngrp <- 1000; nobs <- 2000; phi <- 0.1

ngrp <- 1000; nobs <- 20000; phi <- 0.1

set.seed(101)

dd0 <- simfun0(nobs=nobs, ngrp=ngrp)

dd <- data.frame(dd0,y=rnbinom(nobs,size=phi,mu=dd0$mu))

set.seed(101)

inlam1 <- inla(y~x+f(f,model="iid"),family=list(family="nbinomial"),

                   data=dd, num.threads=1)

summary(inlam1)

set.seed(101)

inlam2 <- inla(y~x+f(f,model="iid"),family=list(family="nbinomial"),

                   data=dd, num.threads=1)

summary(inlam2)

set.seed(101)

inlam3 <- inla(y~x+f(f,model="iid"),family=list(family="nbinomial"),

                   data=dd, num.threads=6)

summary(inlam3)

set.seed(101)

inlam4 <- inla(y~x+f(f,model="iid"),family=list(family="nbinomial"),

                   data=dd, num.threads=6)

summary(inlam4)


In the example, inlam1 and inlam2 are almost identical. Below is one instance of the inconsistent behavior of inlam3 and inlam4

parts:
Hi,

in the INLA algorithm there is an optimization within an optimization.
and the initial value for the inner optimisation is previous optimum.
the issue is when running this in parallel then esentiallt the initial
value is kind of random due to the thread id. this can lead to minor
differences, but in your case more large ones. the way out is to set to
inner optimisation tolerance to something insane small, like

control.inla = list(tolerance = 1e-12)

then it will stop when it cannot improve the inner optimstion any more.

let me know if this does not fix your problem. I would also recommend
to update to the most recent testing version.

Best
H

On Sun, 2017-04-09 at 10:40 -0700, Mollie Brooks wrote:
>
> Thanks for looking into this. I updated to the test version of INLA
> and changed the tolerance as you suggested. The estimates I get are
> much closer to the true values, but they still aren't consistent.
>

thanks for your email.
I looked over it again and ran with your original settings.

your experiments is way to extreme which is what is causing the
problems. the stdev of 5 is highly unreaslistic and leads to range in
mu from 0 to 1E9. this is causing the numerical issues and you see this
also with long running times since it tries to resolve an 'infinity'
issue. when I change to more realistic settings, its way better. I
edited the code somewhat and added also proper priors for the fixed
effects. the 'rerun' is there just to check.

let me know if this is ok with you

H
